headlines.title: NHTSA head Jonathan Morrison speech at AI Horizons PGH Summit Sept. 17, 2026

stage1.korean_title: 미국 NHTSA, 자동화 차량 규제 프레임워크 개정 추진
stage1.korean_summary: 미국 NHTSA가 2017년 자동화 차량 규제(AV 2.0)를 업데이트하여 설계 사양 중심에서 안전 성능 중심으로 FMVSS 규칙을 개정하고 있다.

headlines.body: Morrison gave an important presentation at the Horizons PGH Summit with an update on their Federal Automated Vehicle Framwork. The NHTSA AV 2.0 voluntary guidance document was written in 2017, so they are updating it they are focusing on critical safety elements, such as emergency responder interactions, safety management systems, and remote assistance. "many of our regulations were designed when no one envisioned a vehicle without a human driver, and therefore require or reference manual controls. This means that the technology of the future is often tethered to the regulations of the past. So we are working diligently on much-needed FMVSS updates to account for new designs enabled by automated driving systems, without compromising safety." "by updating the rules to prioritize safety performance requirements over design specifications, we restore common sense to our vehicle regulations." " if we revise our FMVSS to focus on performance, not design requirements, we won’t need to be fortune tellers. Our FMVSSs will be nimble enough to ensure that the vehicles of the future continue to deliver the high level of safety we expect." "We’ve proposed amendments to five critical FMVSS that would have no detrimental effect on safety but would enable creative vehicle designs, and we have many more coming. Our fantastic team of engineers and lawyers is working diligently, with deliberative urgency, to deliver these final rules in a thoughtful manner." How do we know if an AV is a safe driver? "In March, I announced plans to commence development of a Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard for Automated Driving System performance." "I’m excited to announce that just yesterday, we’ve just executed a cooperative agreement with SAE to launch ASCEND consortium. " Morrison also addressed the need for the ASCEND consortium in his presentation to the SAE ATS gathering July 30 in San Diego. "This joint government and industry initiative will expedite the development of data-driven AV performance standards. Our top priority for the consortium is ADS competency, which will inform and accelerate a corresponding FMVSS." "Ultimately, our ADS performance rulemaking will provide federal leadership in this space. By delivering an AV competency standard, we hope we’ll be able to address the burgeoning patchwork of inconsistent State and local level requirements." submitted by /u/CDpov [link] [comments]
